brief.goal: Finish the remaining behavior-owned test migration and lock in the verification CPU gains from TASK-2622.
brief.why: The wave left numeric task-owned tests and permissive or missing CPU limits. Future missions must extend stable behavior owners and fail on CPU regressions without brittle wall-time limits under concurrent load.
brief.scope: Migrate remaining numeric task-ID suites, case modules and helpers by assertion ownership; consolidate compatible groups and split mixed contracts; preserve assertions, task provenance, tiers, isolation and cleanup. Add default authoring/discovery guards. Retune existing unit CPU ceilings and add integration-case and suite CPU limits, including hook command descendants and teardown, from measured plain/covered costs with margin. Attach actual verification and dispositions to the parent.
outOfScope: Changing ports-and-adapters principles, typed application ports, dependency direction, composition authority or adapter boundaries.
Claiming pinned-baseline coverage parity, 50% whole-verification savings or doubled concurrent throughput without separately matched parent evidence.
Weakening required integration gates, E2E obligations, skip policy, unit headroom, watchdogs or fixture cleanup.
